article.author: Valerii Karpov
article.dek: OpenAI is testing Sponsored Agents with select US advertisers while expanding ChatGPT Ads internationally. Paid brand conversations and independent answers are different channels.
article.evidence: OpenAI’s September 16 announcement describes a test with select US advertisers in which a user may start a clearly labelled brand conversation after clicking a ChatGPT ad. We have not run a campaign or observed advertiser results.
article.facts: OpenAI’s September 16 announcement describes a test with select US advertisers in which a user may start a clearly labelled brand conversation after clicking a ChatGPT ad. We have not run a campaign or observed advertiser results.
article.interpretation:
A paid brand conversation and a source cited in an independent answer have different origins. Keep their budgets, disclosure and measurements separate. Combining them into one “AI visibility” number can hide what the business actually bought.

For a future paid test, define a qualified enquiry, the handoff to a person and a spending limit. For organic visibility, record owned pages, dated questions, markets and observed citations. Neither an impression nor an opened conversation is a sale.
article.limits: The September 23 expansion of ChatGPT Ads does not establish that Sponsored Agents are available outside the initial US test, or that a campaign would perform well. Paid placement does not influence ChatGPT’s independent answers.
article.mediaRights: The 48 section scenes and paired Studio workbench are documented staged generated illustrations, not factual photographs or test screenshots. Provenance/rights evidence for the original article covers, OG derivatives, logo and remaining shipped artwork is incomplete. This content-only export records that unresolved state; it is not a media-rights certification or public release approval.
article.practicalDecision: WATCH Sponsored Agents unless your business is eligible for the announced select-US test. PASS on “organic ChatGPT placement” promises based on an ad pilot. Paid and independent-answer visibility need separate measures.

sections.heading: What OpenAI announced
paragraphs: OpenAI’s September 16 announcement describes Sponsored Agents as a test with select US advertisers: a user clicks an ad and may enter a labelled brand conversation. The paid conversation is separate from ChatGPT’s independent answer. No VKV campaign or advertiser result is reported.

A September 23 announcement described broader international ChatGPT Ads availability. Access to that ad platform does not establish access to the Sponsored Agents format, nor a campaign outcome. Check eligibility for the exact format, not just the platform name.

sections.heading: Keep paid and organic claims apart
paragraphs: A paid brand conversation and a source cited in an independent answer have different origins. Keep their budgets, disclosure and measurements separate. Combining them into one “AI visibility” number can hide what the business actually bought.

For a future paid test, define a qualified enquiry, the handoff to a person and a spending limit. For organic visibility, record owned pages, dated questions, markets and observed citations. Neither an impression nor an opened conversation is a sale.

sections.heading: What a business can do now
paragraphs: WATCH in France, Sweden, Finland, the UK and Slovenia: the source cited here does not establish Sponsored Agents access in those markets. In the US, WATCH unless the exact advertiser eligibility is confirmed. This is a dated source description, not a live account-availability check.

ACT on clear product facts and a reachable human contact path. PASS on a supplier presenting this paid pilot as guaranteed independent-answer placement. If a paid trial becomes available, compare qualified enquiries against your own baseline rather than adopting someone else’s campaign results.
